tagline: A cloud computing platform that puts data and artificial intelligence at its core
hero_kpi_rationale: The net revenue retention rate of 125% (2026) demonstrates Snowflake's exceptional ability to generate organic growth from its existing customer base, a key indicator of platform usage expansion and value delivered to customers.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by the Snowflake platform during the fiscal year
kpis.description: Total company revenue for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, reaching $4.7 billion, up 31% compared to the prior year

kpis.name: Total Number of Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of customers using the Snowflake platform
kpis.description: Total number of customers as of January 31, 2026, reaching 13,328 customers, up 21% from 10,996 customers in the prior year

kpis.name: Forbes Global 2000 Customers
kpis.explanation: Number of customers among the world's largest enterprises (Forbes Global 2000)
kpis.description: 790 customers from the Forbes Global 2000 as of January 31, 2026, representing approximately 43% of total revenue for fiscal year 2026

kpis.name: Net Revenue Retention Rate
kpis.explanation: Measure of revenue growth generated by an existing cohort of customers, including expansion and churn
kpis.description: Net revenue retention rate of 125% as of January 31, 2026, compared to 126% the prior year, demonstrating strong expansion capability despite a slight decline

kpis.name: Cloud Regional Deployments
kpis.explanation: Number of regional deployments of the Snowflake platform across major public clouds
kpis.description: 53 regional deployments across three major public cloud providers, enabling a consistent and global user experience

kpis.name: Fiscal Revenue 2025
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated during the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025
kpis.description: $3.6 billion in total revenue for fiscal year 2025, up 29% from $2.8 billion in fiscal year 2024

kpis.name: Number of Customers 2025
kpis.explanation: Total number of customers as of January 31, 2025
kpis.description: 10,996 customers as of January 31, 2025, a solid base that enabled 21% growth to reach 13,328 customers in 2026

risks.title: Future profitability loss due to persistent operating losses
risks.score_rationale: The risk is placed at the top of the document and mentions increasing net losses despite revenue growth. The language emphasizes uncertainty around future profitability, with an accumulated deficit of $9.5 billion in 2026. The Capital category is highly weighted here as it affects long-term viability.

risks.title: Increased competition from cloud giants (AWS, Azure, GCP)
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed across multiple paragraphs and highlights that cloud providers, while also partners, are direct competitors with significantly greater resources. The text mentions risks of pricing bias, bundling, and exclusion. The intensity of the language and length of the section indicate an existential threat.

risks.title: Dependence on consumption-based model with limited financial predictability
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly identified as a major limitation to financial predictability. The consumption model makes revenue forecasting difficult compared to traditional subscription models. This affects investor confidence and earnings stability.

risks.title: Difficulty innovating amid accelerating technological change and AI
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeated multiple times, particularly with the rise of AI. Snowflake depends on its innovation pace to remain competitive. The text mentions challenges related to talent, GPUs, and external models, with alarming language on the consequences of failure.

risks.title: Risks from open data formats and reduced customer lock-in
risks.score_rationale: The shift to open formats like Apache Iceberg is presented as a double-edged sword: it attracts customers but reduces switching costs to competitors. This weakens customer retention and increases competitive pressure.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP)
risks.score_rationale: Snowflake does not operate its own cloud and relies entirely on the three major providers. The text highlights risks of high costs, failure to meet minimum commitments, and vulnerability to strategic decisions by these partner-competitors.

risks.title: Growing regulatory risks in regulated industries
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions increased costs and risks related to regulated markets (healthcare, finance, public sector). Expansion into these areas entails greater compliance, data sovereignty, and security obligations.

ai_positioning.summary: The company Snow does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
